# Psalm 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Why, YHWH, do-You-stand at-a-distance? [Why] do-You-hide in-times of-distress?

**2** In-the-arrogance of-the-wicked he-hotly-pursues the-afflicted; let-them-be-caught in-the-schemes which they-have-devised.

**3** For the-wicked boasts of-the-desire of-his-soul, and-the-greedy-one blesses [himself]; he-spurns YHWH.

**4** The-wicked [says] in-the-height of-his-nose, 'He-does-not seek [it out]'; 'There-is-no God' — all his-thoughts.

**5** His-ways prosper at-every time; on-high [are] Your-judgments, far-from-him; all his-adversaries — he-puffs at-them.

**6** He-says in-his-heart, 'I-shall-not be-moved; from-generation to-generation [I shall be] in-no adversity.'

**7** His-mouth is-full-of cursing and-deceit and-oppression; under his-tongue [are] trouble and-iniquity.

**8** He-sits in-the-ambush of-the-villages; in-the-hiding-places he-murders the-innocent; his-eyes spy-out the-helpless.

**9** He-lurks in-a-hiding-place like-a-lion in-a-thicket; he-lurks to-catch the-afflicted; he-catches the-afflicted when-he-draws-him in-his-net.

**10** He-crushes, he-crouches, and-the-helpless fall by-his-mighty-ones.

**11** He-says in-his-heart, 'God has-forgotten; He-has-hidden His-face; He-will-never see.'

**12** Arise, YHWH! O-God, lift-up Your-hand! Do-not forget the-afflicted.

**13** Why does-the-wicked spurn God? He-says in-his-heart, 'You-will-not seek [it out].'

**14** You-have-seen, for You observe trouble and-grief, to-take [it] in-Your-hand. Upon-You the-helpless commits [himself]; [for] the-orphan You have-been a-helper.

**15** Break the-arm of-the-wicked and-the-evil [one]; seek-out his-wickedness until-You-find none.

**16** YHWH [is] king forever and-ever; the-nations have-perished from-His-land.

**17** The-desire of-the-humble You-have-heard, YHWH; You-strengthen their-heart; You-incline Your-ear,

**18** to-do-justice [for] the-orphan and-the-oppressed, that-no-longer may-man of-the-earth cause-terror.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **10:1**: Psalms 9-10 were originally one acrostic poem (visible in the LXX numbering). The shift from praise (Ps 9) to lament (Ps 10) is deliberate.

- **10:4**: 'Height of his nose' — the Hebrew idiom for arrogance. Pride is literally 'having one's nose in the air.'

— EMET
